sections.h2: Where is Wheeling, WV, and why is its housing stock so old?
sections.html:
Wheeling is the seat of Ohio County and the largest city in West Virginia's Northern Panhandle, lying along the Ohio River about 11 miles west of Pennsylvania. Wikipedia gives a 2020 population of 27,062, fifth in the state, and a metro population of 139,513. Parts of the city lie in Marshall County.

The city grew early. It was the endpoint of the National Road, and the Wheeling Suspension Bridge, completed in 1849, linked downtown with Wheeling Island. The Baltimore and Ohio Railroad arrived in 1853. Wheeling hosted the conventions that led to West Virginia's separation from Virginia, and it served as the state capital from 1861 to 1870 and again from 1875 to 1885.

Population peaked at 61,659 in the 1930 census and has fallen since heavy industry declined. Wikipedia notes that prosperous residents built fine houses, especially on Wheeling Island, during the growth years. Housing from those decades remains, so ask for a full condition review of any older Wheeling house.

The city covers 16.01 square miles, of which 13.79 are land, and Wheeling Creek runs through it to meet the Ohio River downtown.

sections.h2: Which Wheeling neighborhoods are most distinct?
sections.html:
Wheeling has dozens of named neighborhoods, and the hillsides and the island create very different settings. The list on Wikipedia includes several that sellers often mention:

  • Wheeling Island, in the middle of the Ohio River
  • North Wheeling, East Wheeling, South Wheeling and Center Wheeling
  • Warwood, Woodsdale, Oakmont and Pleasant Valley
  • Oglebay Park, Park View and Wheeling Heights
  • Arbordale, Pleasanton, Springdale and Dimmeydale

Some neighborhoods, such as Benwood, Mozart, Mount Olivet and Sherrard, are partly or mostly in Marshall County, so an address that says Wheeling may be billed by a different county. Always confirm the county before you look up taxes.

The city also has a North Wheeling Design Review process and a Historic Landmarks Commission. If your house is in a historic area, ask the Building and Planning department whether exterior changes need review before you commit to repairs.

sections.h2: What flood risk should a Wheeling seller expect?
sections.html:
Flood zones in Wheeling are common. The city's Building and Planning FAQ says property along the Ohio River, Wheeling Creek and its larger tributaries is in the flood zone, and that every ward in the city contains flood zones. To check a specific property, enter the address in the state's flood map tool.

The city's Building Code Official also serves as floodplain manager, and the department lists NFIP floodplain development guidelines on its building code services page. Fences in the floodplain need a building permit, which is a detail owners often miss.

QuestionCity answer
Where are flood zones?Along the Ohio River, Wheeling Creek and larger tributaries
Which wards have them?Every ward
Who manages the floodplain?The Building Code Official, as floodplain manager
Is a permit needed for a fence?Yes, for fences in the floodplain

For a seller, the practical step is to find out your flood zone status before you accept an offer, since lenders and insurers use it. Annual precipitation in Wheeling averages about 41.88 inches, spread evenly through the year, per Wikipedia.

sections.h2: What are Wheeling's vacant building and demolition rules?
sections.html:
Wheeling requires owners of vacant structures to register them, and neglected buildings can be ordered repaired or razed. The Vacant Structure Code, adopted by City Council in 2009, tracks ownership and encourages maintenance. Once a building is registered, the owner has a year to renovate and occupy it, tear it down or sell it before a fee is assessed, and fees increase for each year the building stays vacant.

The Building Code Services page explains the enforcement side. Owners must either maintain or raze their buildings. Irresponsible owners may receive a Raze or Repair Order, and failure to comply can mean a Municipal Court appearance and a monetary penalty. Where public health and safety are at risk, the city may raze the structure and place a lien on the property for the cost, without taking ownership.

  • A vacant registered building gets one year before fees start.
  • Fees rise each year the building stays vacant.
  • A city demolition becomes a lien against the property.

The sale option matters here. The program says an owner can sell within the first year without a fee, so a prompt sale can stop the clock. If you inherited a vacant Wheeling house, that is worth knowing early. Cash Home Buyers reviews houses as is, including ones that need major work, and you owe nothing if you decline.

sections.h2: What permits and codes apply to repairs on a Wheeling house?
sections.html:
The city uses the 2018 International Building and Residential Codes and the 2018 International Property Maintenance Code, with the 2020 National Electric Code. A building permit costs $4.00 per $1,000 of job cost, rounded up to the next $1,000, so a $5,600 project costs $24.00. A new electric service adds a $25 residential fee.

Most applications are reviewed within 48 hours, and larger projects can take up to a week. Roofing, siding and window permits can sometimes be issued the same day. Permits are required for work that sellers commonly consider before listing:

  • A new roof, siding or kitchen and bathroom renovation
  • Electrical upgrades and new decks
  • Garage or carport construction
  • Fences in the floodplain or over 7 feet
  • Retaining walls over 48 inches

Unpermitted work can surface in a buyer's inspection and slow a sale. The city also notes that it cannot use federal community development funds for home repairs on pre 1970 construction because of lead based paint rules, so there is no city repair grant to count on. A buyer who purchases as is avoids that repair path altogether.

sections.h2: How does property tax work for a Wheeling house?
sections.html:
Ohio County's Sheriff's Tax Office collects real estate and personal property taxes, and the County Assessor values the property. The tax office is at 1500 Chapline Street, Room 206, and the office page lists these deadlines:

  • September 1: first half discount ends
  • October 1: first half taxes become delinquent and interest begins
  • March 1: second half discount ends
  • April 1: second half taxes become delinquent
  • April 30: unpaid taxes are subject to publication and added fees
  • October 31: unpaid delinquent real estate taxes are certified to the state auditor

Statements are mailed in July. You can search records and pay online at wvpropertytaxes.com, where the office lists a $1.00 fee for electronic checks and $1.00 plus 2.2 percent for cards.

Statewide, assessed value is 60 percent of market value, according to the Wood County assessor's explanation of the same state system, and the first $20,000 of assessed value of an owner occupied home is exempt for owners 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled. See the Tax Division exemption list.

sections.h2: What will closing a Wheeling sale cost in transfer taxes?
sections.html:
The deed is taxed under West Virginia's transfer excise tax, which the seller normally pays. Under section 11-22-2, the rate is $1.10 for each $500 of value, plus a county excise tax of 55 cents per $500 that a county commission can raise, and a $20 fee for the Affordable Housing Fund.

On an $80,000 sale, the base $1.10 rate comes to $176, and adding the 55 cent county tax brings it to $264. That is arithmetic from the statute, not a quote. Deeds are recorded by the Ohio County Clerk.

Transfers by will or through a list of heirs are excluded under section 11-22-1.

sections.h2: How do roads and transit connect Wheeling?
sections.html:
I-70 and I-470 run through the city and link it with Pittsburgh's suburbs and Ohio, and US 40, US 250 and WV Route 2 also serve it. The Fort Henry Bridge carries I-70 across the river, and the interstate passes under Wheeling Hill through the Wheeling Tunnel. The county also runs the Wheeling Ohio County Airport.

The Robert C. Byrd Intermodal Transportation Center is the hub for Greyhound and for regional bus service run by the Ohio Valley Regional Transit Authority.

faqs.q: What happens if my Wheeling house has been vacant for over a year?
faqs.a: Under the city's Vacant Structure Code, registered owners get a year before a fee is assessed, and fees rise each year the building stays vacant. Selling is one of the allowed ways to resolve it.

faqs.q: Is my Wheeling house in a flood zone?
faqs.a: The city says every ward contains flood zones, mostly along the Ohio River, Wheeling Creek and larger tributaries. Enter your address in the state flood map tool to check.

faqs.q: When are Ohio County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1. First half taxes become delinquent October 1, and second half taxes April 1.

faqs.q: What is a Raze or Repair Order?
faqs.a: It is a notice from the city's Building Inspection division requiring an owner to repair or demolish a building. Ignoring it can lead to Municipal Court and a lien for the city's demolition cost.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax on a Wheeling sale?
faqs.a: The seller normally pays it unless the buyer accepts the deed without it being paid. The state rate is $1.10 per $500, with a county tax starting at 55 cents per $500.
